turns.doctor_question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, it's nice to meet you too. Thanks for seeing me. Um, I guess I'm just here because work has been a little... well, maybe just a bit more scattered lately than usual? I'm an electrician, and usually I'm really good at my job, I promise. But lately, I don't know, it's just been a little harder to keep my focus on one estimate or code form at a time. 

It's nothing terrible, really, just... if I hear a tool noise, or get a text, or even if I just get a really great new idea about how to organize the workshop, I just sort of get pulled off track. And then, you know, some of the jobs have started getting a little mixed up. I hope that makes sense? I just want to get back to being reliable, you know?

symptom_reasoning.S001: The patient mentions that jobs are getting mixed up as a result of losing focus, indicating careless mistakes or errors.
symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient explicitly states it has been harder to keep focus on one estimate or code form at a time, showing difficulty sustaining attention.
symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient describes being easily distracted by extraneous stimuli like tool noises and texts, as well as unrelated thoughts like new ideas for the workshop.
symptom_reasoning.S039: The patient reports that their attention is easily drawn to irrelevant external stimuli (tool noises, texts) and internal thoughts, pulling them off track.

turns.doctor_question: When you think back to childhood, were you already someone who got distracted easily?
turns.patient_response:
Um, no, actually. Not really. When I think back, I was always pretty good at paying attention in school, I think. I mean, I really tried my best to be a good student and listen to my teachers. I definitely wasn't one of those kids bouncing off the walls or anything, I promise. 

This whole... scattered thing, it really feels pretty new for me. It's not how I usually am at all. Is that okay? I hope that's the kind of information you were looking for.

symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient states they were always good at paying attention in school, denying a history of difficulty sustaining attention.
symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient explicitly denies being someone who got distracted easily during childhood.
symptom_reasoning.S014: The patient denies being hyperactive or 'bouncing off the walls' as a child.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling unusually energetic or 'up' lately?
turns.patient_response:
Well, I guess... maybe a little bit? I mean, I've definitely had a lot of energy, but I've always been a hard worker, you know? It's just that lately, I get these big, exciting ideas. Like, I'll be in this really pumped-up mood, just feeling great, and I'll start talking about how our little shop is going to become the main solar outfit in the whole town. It's a good vision, right? 

But, um, I guess the downside is... well, if my wife or one of the apprentices questions the plan, even just a little bit, I can sometimes... flip, I guess? I might get a little sharp with them over practically nothing. I feel terrible about it afterwards, I really do. I don't mean to snap, it's just that I get so passionate about the ideas. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making myself sound awful... I'm really trying to be better about it.

symptom_reasoning.S033: The patient describes being in a 'pumped-up mood' and feeling great, but also admits to flipping and getting sharp with others, indicating both elevated and irritable mood.
symptom_reasoning.S034: The patient explicitly states having 'a lot of energy' lately.
symptom_reasoning.S035: The patient describes having 'big, exciting ideas' and grand visions of their small shop becoming the main solar outfit in town, indicating inflated self-esteem or grandiosity.
symptom_reasoning.S060: The patient admits to snapping and getting 'a little sharp' with their wife or apprentices over 'practically nothing', showing low frustration tolerance and snappiness.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been needing less sleep than usual?
turns.patient_response:
Um, I suppose my sleep has changed a little bit, but honestly, it hasn't been a problem at all. For a few months now, I've been getting maybe... three or four hours a night? But I don't feel tired, I promise. I pop up way before dawn and I just feel completely refreshed, like I had a full night's rest. 

It's actually been really great for catching up on work. I use that quiet time to price out materials, answer my emails, or, you know, sketch out another system design for the shop. I just figured I was being super productive and dedicated to the business. That's a good thing, right? I hope it's okay that my schedule is a little weird right now...

symptom_reasoning.S036: The patient reports sleeping only three or four hours a night but feeling completely refreshed and not tired.
symptom_reasoning.S040: The patient describes using the extra waking hours to engage in work-related tasks like pricing materials, answering emails, and sketching designs, indicating increased goal-directed activity.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling unusually confident or like you can do things that are beyond what you’d normally expect of yourself?
turns.patient_response:
Well, I... I guess I have been feeling pretty capable lately. Like, really capable. I've been having these thoughts that I could start taking on big commercial jobs, you know? And maybe even hire and train a whole crew right now to handle it all. 

I mean, I know it sounds like a lot, and... well, if I'm being completely honest, there's a part of me that knows my licensing and my actual experience aren't quite at that level yet. I'm just an electrician, and I haven't done much commercial work at all. But when I get in those moods, it just feels so doable, like I'm meant to be doing it. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound arrogant or anything. I just want to grow the business and do a good job. Is it normal to get a little ahead of yourself when you're feeling good like that?

symptom_reasoning.S035: The patient describes feeling unusually capable and believing they can take on large commercial jobs and train a crew, despite acknowledging they lack the necessary licensing and experience, indicating inflated self-esteem and overestimation of abilities.

turns.doctor_question: Have you done anything unusually risky lately, like spending a lot of money or taking on major commitments you normally wouldn’t?
turns.patient_response:
Um, risky? No, I wouldn't say I've done anything like that. I mean, I try to be really responsible, especially with the business and my wife, you know? I haven't gone out and bought a sports car or gambled our savings away or anything crazy like that. 

I guess I've maybe bought a few extra tools for the shop lately, just trying to be prepared for when things pick up, but... that's just normal business expenses, right? I always try to keep things reasonable. I hope that's what you mean? I really don't think I've been doing anything too out there.

symptom_reasoning.S041: The patient explicitly denies engaging in unusually risky behaviors, such as unrestrained buying or gambling, stating they try to be responsible and keep things reasonable.

turns.doctor_question: Have these high-energy, pumped-up periods been happening as a distinct stretch of time that feels different from your usual self?
turns.patient_response:
Well, I... I guess they do happen in stretches, yeah. It definitely feels a bit different from my normal day-to-day. Like, I'll get into this really big, pumped-up mood, you know? I'll start talking about how our little shop is going to expand and become the main solar outfit in the whole town. It just feels so exciting and positive.

But, um... I guess there's another side to it that I'm not super proud of. If my wife or one of the apprentices questions my plan when I'm like that, or even just asks a simple question about how it's going to work... I can kind of flip. I get a little sharp with them over practically nothing. 

I always feel terrible about it after. I don't mean to snap at them, I just get so focused and passionate about the ideas. It's just the stress of running a business, I think. That happens to a lot of guys, right? Getting a little irritable when you're under pressure? I really try to keep it in check, I promise.

symptom_reasoning.S033: The patient confirms experiencing distinct stretches of a 'pumped-up mood' that feels different from their normal self, along with irritability when questioned.
symptom_reasoning.S035: The patient exhibits inflated self-confidence and grandiosity by claiming their small shop will expand to become the main solar outfit in town.
symptom_reasoning.S060: The patient admits to reacting sharply and becoming irritable over minor stimuli, such as simple questions from his wife or apprentices.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?
turns.patient_response:
Depressed? Oh, um... no, I don't think so. Not like that, anyway. I mean, everybody gets a little down sometimes, right? Like if work is slow or things are stressful at home, I might feel a bit tired or just... you know, not my best self for a couple of days. 

But two whole weeks of feeling bad most of the day? No, I really don't think I've ever had anything like that. I try to stay positive and keep moving forward. I'm usually pretty good at just shaking it off and getting back to work. I hope that's the right answer? I just don't want you to think I'm the kind of guy who just gives up and mopes around. I always try to push through.

symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient explicitly denies ever experiencing a period of feeling depressed most of the day for two weeks.

turns.doctor_question: During one of these pumped-up periods, have you ever been hospitalized because of your mood or behavior?
turns.patient_response:
Hospitalized? Oh, gosh, no. No, never anything like that. I mean, I know sometimes people get a little carried away when they're excited, but I've never been out of control or anything where I needed to be in a hospital. 

I really try to be responsible and manage my stress before it ever gets to a point like that. I've always been able to just stay at home and keep working through it. That means I'm doing okay, right? I just want to make sure you know I'm not, like, a danger to myself or anyone else. I always try to keep a lid on things.

turns.doctor_question: During one of these pumped-up periods, has it ever gotten so severe that you couldn't do your job or take care of things at home?
turns.patient_response:
Well, I... I wouldn't say I couldn't do my job. I mean, I'm always out there working, you know? I never just stop. But, um... I guess things have gotten a little... messy, sometimes. I don't want to make it sound worse than it is, but we've had a few clients complain lately. Just about some missed details, or me getting the scheduling mixed up when I'm moving really fast. And my apprentices, they... well, they don't seem to trust my direction the way they used to. Which is hard to admit, because I really try to be a good boss for them. 

And at home... I'm still trying to take care of everything, I promise. But my wife and I, we've been getting into these constant arguments. It's mostly about the mortgage and the business. She... she feels like I'm putting everything we've built at risk when I get so geared up about expanding. I hate upsetting her. I'm just trying to provide for us, you know? Every small business owner goes through rough patches with scheduling and family stress, right? I'm still doing okay, aren't I?

symptom_reasoning.S001: The patient admits to clients complaining about 'missed details' in his work.
symptom_reasoning.S005: The patient mentions getting scheduling mixed up, indicating difficulty organizing tasks.
symptom_reasoning.S014: The patient describes himself as 'always out there working,' 'moving really fast,' and says 'I never just stop,' reflecting constant activity.
symptom_reasoning.S040: The patient describes getting 'geared up about expanding' his business and constantly working, indicating increased goal-directed activity.
symptom_reasoning.S041: The patient's wife feels he is putting everything they've built at risk with his business expansion and mortgage decisions, indicating involvement in activities with painful consequences.
